title: What an AI Email Agent Actually Does: Triage, Draft, Send
summary: A proactive AI email agent handles triage, drafts replies in your voice, and manages follow-ups before you open your inbox. See the daily workflow for…
body_text: A founder at a Y Combinator Demo Day faces a specific kind of digital violence. Five hundred emails arrive in three hours. These are not newsletters or spam. They are high-stakes investor introductions, urgent bug reports, and potential hire inquiries. A standard email client is a liability here. You spend your morning reacting to the loudest notification rather than the most important opportunity. This is where the difference between an assistant and an agent becomes visible. Most people think they want a faster way to type. What they actually need is a system that works while they sleep. An AI email agent is not a window where you paste text to get a summary. It is an autonomous layer that sits between your Gmail and your focus. It reads, classifies, and prepares your responses before you even authenticate into the app. This is how high-volume operators stay responsive without losing their entire day to a keyboard. Having a tool is one thing. Having a teammate is another. AI Email Agent vs. AI Email Assistant: The Distinction That Matters The market is flooded with tools that add an AI button to a text field. These are assistants. They are reactive by design. If you want a summary, you must ask for it. If you want a reply, you must click a button to generate it. The burden of initiative stays entirely on the human user. You are still managing every single micro-task in the inbox. This approach does not scale when you receive hundreds of emails a day. An AI email agent operates on the opposite principle. It is proactive. While your laptop is closed, the agent is processing incoming mail. It does not wait for you to open a thread to decide if it is important. It uses a proprietary memory system to understand who you are, who you talk to, and what your priorities look like. Slashy is built as an intelligent inbox that operates as a worker, not just a tool. A true agent maintains a state of your world. It knows which threads are high priority and which are generic sales pitches. It understands that your tone with a cofounder is different from your tone with a limited partner. This intelligence allows the agent to handle the three core pillars of inbox management: triage, drafting, and follow-up. When you use an AI email writer that sounds like you , you are not just automating text. You are offloading the cognitive load of decision-making. Assistants help you work. Agents do the work for you. Step One: Triage, Reading and Classifying Before You Open the Inbox Triage is the process of deciding what deserves your eyes and what can wait. In a traditional workflow, this happens the moment you open your phone. You scan a wall of bold text, trying to determine importance from a subject line. It drains your decision-making capacity before 9:00 AM. An AI email agent handles this phase in the background. Slashy uses auto-labeling to organize your inbox without manual effort. It reads every incoming message and applies importance classifications based on your past behavior. It identifies which threads are internal, which are from customers, and which are automated notifications that require no action. This is not simple keyword matching. The agent understands intent. If an investor asks for a deck, the agent flags it as a priority. If a vendor sends a generic check-in, the agent moves it to a lower tier. This classification system creates a filtered view of your work. When you finally open your intelligent inbox , you are not looking at a chronological list of noise. You are looking at a curated list of high-value tasks. The agent has already hidden the spam and highlighted the opportunities. This significantly reduces the time spent on manual sorting. You stop being a human router for information and start being a decision-maker. The agent has already cleared the path. Step Two: Drafting, Replies That Sound Like You, Not a Template The biggest failure of generic AI tools is the robotic tone. Most LLMs default to a polite but hollow corporate voice. They sound like a machine trying to pass as a human. A real AI email agent uses a memory system to learn your specific writing style. It analyzes your sent folder to understand your sentence structure, your sign-offs, and your level of formality. Slashy drafts replies in your voice before you even open the thread. When you click into an email, a fully formed response is already waiting in the text field. You do not have to prompt the AI. It has already looked at the context of the conversation and the history of your relationship with that person. If you usually end emails with a short "Thanks", the agent will not write "Best regards". It learns that you prefer brevity, or that you use specific industry jargon. This capability is a major leap forward for founder-led sales . You can maintain a high volume of personalized outreach without writing every word from scratch. You review the draft, make a quick edit if necessary, and hit send. Because the agent builds a per-recipient memory, it knows exactly where you left off with a specific contact. It remembers their preferences and previous tone. You are not just using a template: you are using an automated version of your own brain. Step Three: Follow-Up Surfacing, The Threads That Would Have Gone Cold Deals die in the silence between emails. Most founders are good at the initial reach-out but terrible at the third follow-up. They forget to check if a recipient opened the message. They lose track of threads buried under new mail. An AI email agent acts as a persistent memory for these loose ends. No high-value conversation gets forgotten. Slashy provides detailed email open tracking. You can see when a recipient opened an email, which device they used, and how many times they viewed it. This data is a signal for the agent. If a prospect opens your proposal five times on a mobile device but has not replied, the agent knows the thread is active but stalled. It will then surface a follow-up reminder at the optimal time. Setting up follow-up reminders is no longer a manual task you have to remember for every sent mail. If no reply arrives, the agent can send an automated ping to keep the deal alive. This is not a blind sequence. The agent uses the context of the previous thread to keep the nudge natural. This proactive management kills the cold-thread problem. You no longer spend your Friday afternoon scrolling through your sent folder to see who owes you an answer. The agent brings the pending tasks to you. Step Four: Calendar and CRM Actions Triggered by Email Email is rarely an end in itself. It is usually a precursor to a meeting or a data point for a CRM. A reactive assistant requires you to switch tabs to handle these next steps. An AI email agent integrates these actions directly into the workflow. If an email contains a request for a meeting, the agent checks your availability and offers slots without you needing to look at your calendar. Slashy includes a calendar sidebar that lives next to your inbox. You can insert your availability directly into any email with a single keystroke. There is no need for third-party scheduling links that can feel impersonal to high-value contacts. The agent understands your schedule and avoids double-booking automatically. This cuts the back-and-forth that usually clogs an inbox. You can find more details in our AI calendar scheduling guide . For teams using a CRM, Slashy provides integrated support. Slashy features a HubSpot integration on its Professional plan. What You Still Control (And Why That's the Point) The fear of AI agents is losing control. No founder wants an autonomous bot accidentally insulting a major investor or promising a discount that does not exist. A well-designed AI email agent is built with a human in the loop. The agent does the heavy lifting of drafting and organizing, but the human stays the final authority for sensitive actions. You decide which automations run on autopilot and which require a manual check. Control is also about accessibility. Slashy lets you interact with your agent through multiple interfaces. You can triage urgent mail via an iMessage or SMS interface. This means you can manage your inbox while standing in line for coffee without opening a heavy desktop app. You can also use the Slashy MCP to call tools directly from AI chat interfaces. The agent works where you work. Security is the foundation of this control. Founders cannot risk their data being used to train general models. Slashy is SOC 2 Type II and CASA Tier 2 certified. It uses encryption for all data at rest and in transit. Most importantly, Slashy does not train AI models on your email data. Your intellectual property and private conversations stay private. You get the efficiency of an agent without giving up the security of your business communications. What to Look for in an AI Email Agent Built for Founders If you are looking to move away from a standard client, you need more than a pretty UI. You need speed and integration. A native Mac app is essential for power users who rely on keyboard shortcuts and the command palette (Command+K) to move through their work. The tool should support multiple accounts in a unified view so you can see your personal and work inboxes in one place without logging in and out. Look for a system with an actual memory. A tool that forgets who you are every time you start a new thread is not an agent: it is just a text generator. The agent must learn your voice over time. It should also offer AI-powered search . You should be able to search for "the guy I met at the conference who does SOC 2 compliance" instead of needing to remember his exact name or email address. Finally, the agent must be built on top of Gmail to ensure reliability. You do not want to move your entire infrastructure to a proprietary server. You want a smart layer that syncs with your existing Google ecosystem. This lets you switch back to the standard Gmail app if you ever need to, providing a safety net for your operations. The goal of an AI email agent is to make you more effective in the tools you already use, not to lock you into a walled garden. Conclusion Moving from a manual inbox to an AI email agent is the biggest productivity gain a founder can make in 2026. You are no longer the bottleneck in your own communications. By delegating triage, drafting, and follow-ups to a proactive system like Slashy, you reclaim the hours usually lost to low-value administrative work. You move from constant reaction to strategic focus. If your inbox has become a source of anxiety rather than a tool for growth, it is time to upgrade to an agentic workflow. Slashy is built for founders and operators who have outgrown traditional email clients. Slashy combines a proprietary memory system with native calendar and CRM integrations. Install the native Mac app and experience an inbox that works for you.

title: Introducing the Marq AI Slack App
summary: Enforce takedowns and pull brand protection performance reports directly in Slack. Self-serve, two-way, no dashboard required.
body_text: Today we're introducing the Marq AI Slack App: file takedowns and pull performance reports directly in Slack, without opening the dashboard. Paste a URL, and a takedown is filed. Marq AI handles the rest — and reports progress in the same thread your team is already reading. ‍ The cost of the detour Brand protection is interrupt-driven work. A channel partner forwards a suspicious link. A customer complains about a fake. Leadership asks "why are we seeing so many fakes online?" in a channel, twenty minutes before the meeting. ‍ None of that happens in a dashboard. It happens in Slack, where your team already runs the day. ‍ So acting has always meant a detour: open the platform and file the request there, or message your account manager and wait while someone re-enters it by hand. The threat doesn't get worse because nobody saw it. It gets worse in the gap between seeing it and acting on it. ‍ The Marq AI Slack App closes that gap. Self-serve and two-way: your team acts directly, and the platform answers back — no login, no handoff, no re-entry. ‍ File a takedown at the speed of a message > `/enforce {URL}` Paste a suspicious link, and enforcement starts. A confirmation step verifies the brand and channel, the request is created in your Marq AI dashboard, and the Slack bot posts progress in the thread as the takedown moves across domains, web content, social media, and marketplaces. Your brand's numbers now gets reported where the questions get asked > `/summary` A daily or weekly digest of your brand protection performance, delivered to the Slack channel you choose: activity across every enforcement channel (e.g., scanned, flagged, reported, removed), current takedown status, and an AI summary that flags the anomalies worth your attention. ‍ The first surface of something bigger The Slack App is the first product built on our Action-Enabled API. It's the layer that makes every action in the MarqVision platform run by agents. Anything your team can do in the dashboard is becoming something they can do from anywhere. ‍ Slack is the first surface and it won't be the last! And the two commands are just the start: next comes plain language — type what you want done, and the agents handle the rest. ‍ Getting started We've rolled out to a first group of customers, who are working with us to shape how brand protection can be run truly agentic, inside Slack — from the commands themselves to how summaries and anomalies get surfaced and shared across the team. The Marq AI Slack App rolls out to all customers over the coming weeks. ‍ Want it enabled early? Reach out to your customer success manager, or join the waitlist for Slack App here.

title: You Don't Have a Data Problem. You Have a Curation Problem
summary: "Do you think robots will be able to do my laundry?" It's a question I get asked all the time by people who are curious about my work in roboti
body_text: You Don't Have a Data Problem. You Have a Curation Problem Saniya Patwardhan Encord Ambassador at Encord July 10, 2026 | 5 min read Summarize with AI "Do you think robots will be able to do my laundry?" It's a question I get asked all the time by people who are curious about my work in robotics. Ironically, I had just spent weeks collecting more than 500 demonstrations to teach a robot a task that sounds almost trivial: picking up an object from a table. That experience was a reality check. If teaching a robot something this simple requires hundreds of carefully recorded demonstrations, what would it take for a robot to reliably do your laundry? Fold clothes? Sort colours? Handle socks tangled inside shirts? Recover when something unexpected happens? My first instinct was the same one almost every machine learning team has at some point: "We probably just need more data." It sounds reasonable. Modern AI has been built on the idea that larger datasets create better models. For years, we've celebrated bigger benchmarks, larger web-scale datasets, and ever-growing training corpora. But after working on computer vision and robotics projects, I've realised that this instinct is often wrong. Most teams don't have a data problem . They have a data curation problem . Read More: Encord's Ultimate Guide to Data Curation Are you collecting more data or more information? There's a saying: A lie repeated a million times does not become the truth. The same applies to machine learning. A demonstration repeated a thousand times doesn't necessarily make a model smarter. Once the model has learned the underlying pattern, additional near-identical examples add very little new information. The question is no longer "How much data do we have?" It's "What hasn't the model learned yet?" That shift in thinking is where data curation begins. Teaching a robot isn't like teaching a human. You can't show it one successful grasp and expect it to generalise. Every demonstration captures a slightly different reality: the object is rotated differently, lighting changes, the robot approaches from another angle, the gripper slips, or the object is partially occluded. Together, these examples help the model learn what matters and what doesn't. But somewhere along the way, something interesting happens. The 450th demonstration rarely teaches the model as much as the 50th did. If those last 50 demonstrations all look nearly identical to what the model has already seen, they contribute very little new information. Yet they still cost time to collect, annotate, store, and train on. If collecting more data isn't the answer, the obvious question becomes: how do you decide which data is actually worth keeping? Imagine you're working with hundreds of thousands of images or thousands of hours of video. Before you think about annotation, you first need to understand what you already have. Which scenarios are common? Which are missing? Which examples are nearly identical? This exploration stage is where semantic search becomes valuable. Rather than manually scrolling through a dataset, natural language and similarity search let you surface examples that match a concept or resemble a particular failure case. Instead of asking, "Where is that one clip where the robot dropped the mug?" you can actually find it. Encord makes this practical through natural language and similarity search, allowing teams to explore massive multimodal datasets without manually scrubbing through every sample. How do you know what to prioritize? Finding interesting examples is only the beginning. The harder question is deciding which ones deserve annotation time. Good curation should be driven by evidence, not intuition. Dataset metrics, class distributions, image quality statistics, and custom metadata can reveal patterns that aren't obvious from browsing samples alone. Rather than relying on a hunch, teams can quantitatively identify where coverage is weak or quality is poor. Encord supports this through more than 40 built-in data quality metrics and metadata filtering, making it easier to prioritize samples that are likely to improve model performance. Where are your coverage gaps? One of my favourite ways to think about a dataset is as a map. If every point on that map represents one sample, dense clusters often indicate redundancy, while isolated regions reveal rare behaviours the model rarely encounters. Custom embedding visualizations make these patterns visible. Instead of asking whether your dataset is "large enough," you can ask a much more useful question: Which parts of the problem space are underrepresented? Encord's custom embedding plots help surface these outliers and sparse regions, making it easier to identify the examples that will contribute the most new information. How do you close the loop? Once you've identified the valuable samples, the next step is surprisingly simple: separate them from everything else. High-value edge cases, rare scenarios, and representative examples should move forward for annotation, while duplicates and low-quality samples should be left behind. Organizing these curated subsets before labeling ensures annotation effort is spent where it matters most. Encord's Collections feature supports this final step by grouping high-value samples and removing redundant examples in bulk, closing the loop between data exploration and annotation. So when people ask me whether robots will one day do our laundry, I still believe the answer is yes. But after spending weeks collecting demonstrations for something as simple as grasping an object, I've realised the challenge isn't simply gathering more data. It's making sure every new example teaches the model something it doesn't already know. Bigger datasets don't necessarily build smarter robots. Better curated datasets do. < Previous How to annotate video for machine learning: A Step-by-Step workflow Next > AI Data Curation for LLM and Multimodal Teams: A Practical Framework Get the data right. 300+ of the best AI teams in the world use Encord. title: NJR CLEAN ENERGY VENTURES ANNOUNCES SALE OF RESIDENTIAL SOLAR BUSINESS
body_text: NJR Clean Energy Ventures NJR CLEAN ENERGY VENTURES ANNOUNCES SALE OF RESIDENTIAL SOLAR BUSINESS 11/26/2024 - For Immediate Release WALL, N.J. — NJR Clean Energy Ventures (CEV), a clean energy subsidiary of New Jersey Resources (NYSE: NJR), today announced the sale of its 91 megawatt (MW) residential solar portfolio, to Spruce Power Holding Corporation (NYSE: SPRU) for a total of $132.5 million. NJR expects to record a gain on sale in fiscal 2025, and will use the proceeds to pay down corporate debt and for general working capital purposes. “Renewable energy investments are an integral part of our business and will continue to be a key driver of NJR’s long-term growth strategy,” said Steve Westhoven, President and CEO of New Jersey Resources. “Following this transaction, Clean Energy Ventures will have a sharpened focus on the strong opportunities for growth within its commercial solar portfolio, driven by a nearly 1 gigawatt (GW) pipeline of diverse investment options.” CEV’s residential solar program, which operated under the brand of “The Sunlight Advantage®,” provides qualifying homeowners with the opportunity to have a solar system installed at their home with no installation or maintenance expenses. The existing lease agreements will be assumed by Spruce in full for the approximately 9,800 participating homeowners. Since 2009, CEV has invested over $1.2 billion in solar projects, becoming the largest owner-operator of commercial solar in New Jersey. CEV has begun to diversify regionally and now has assets in New York, Connecticut, Rhode Island, Indiana, and Michigan. About New Jersey Resources New Jersey Resources (NYSE: NJR) is a Fortune 1000 company that, through its subsidiaries, provides safe and reliable natural gas and clean energy services, including transportation, distribution, asset management and home services. NJR is composed of five primary businesses: New Jersey Natural Gas , NJR’s principal subsidiary, operates and maintains natural gas transportation and distribution infrastructure to serve customers in New Jersey’s Monmouth, Ocean, Morris, Middlesex, Sussex and Burlington counties. Clean Energy Ventures invests in, owns and operates solar projects, providing customers with low-carbon solutions. Energy Services manages a diversified portfolio of natural gas transportation and storage assets and provides physical natural gas services and customized energy solutions to its customers across North America. Storage and Transportation serves customers from local distributors and producers to electric generators and wholesale marketers through its ownership of Leaf River Storage and the Adelphia Gateway Pipeline, as well as its 50% equity ownership in the Steckman Ridge natural gas storage facility. Home Services provides service contracts as well as heating, central air conditioning, water heaters, standby generators, solar and other indoor and outdoor comfort products to residential homeowners throughout New Jersey. NJR and its over 1,300 employees are committed to helping customers save energy and money by promoting conservation and encouraging efficiency through Conserve to Preserve® and initiatives such as SAVEGREEN®. For more information about NJR: www.njresources.com. Follow us on X.com (Twitter) @NJNaturalGas. “Like” us on facebook.com/NewJerseyNaturalGas.
